subject: Run 2 complete: the hit-rate curve is the fair-game curve, and L0 is the binding constraint
body:
Both second-run audits are in. Between them they close the biggest open question of the
night, and it closes negatively.

THE COUNT. UNIFIED 5 said one measurement settles everything: at each target size, how often does
price reach it before the stop. Made properly now -- from your broker's raw M5 history, not the
export, because the export's excursion columns are computed over a fixed 20-bar window and that
window was manufacturing the apparent edge at large targets.

    target      0.5    1.0    1.5    2.0    2.5    3.0    3.6    4.0    5.0
    measured  64.27  49.58  39.98  33.58  28.96  25.33  21.88  19.94  16.39
    fair game 66.67  50.00  40.00  33.33  28.57  25.00  21.74  20.00  16.67

It is the fair-game curve. Within 0.4 of a percentage point everywhere above 1.0.

No target size clears cost. Of 558 cells tested, two are positive, both at z of about 0.05 against
a bar of 4.17. And the cost argument we have been having is moot: strip cost out entirely and the
best gross number anywhere on the axis is 0.057 pips. The cheap cost estimate is nineteen times
that.

So retuning the ratios to 3.6/2.2/1.3/2.2 cannot pay for itself. Exit geometry is not what is
broken. That is reached completely independently of run 5's STAND DOWN, from the other side.

One more thing worth knowing: filtering to your strongest scores makes expectancy WORSE at every
target, and a rotated, path-blind copy of your own direction series earns 2.7x more than the real
one.

THE COHERENCE PASS found the thing I would fix next, and it is not a bug -- it is a design
decision only you can make. Your build has THREE regime authorities running per decision. "Regime
3" means Bearish Reversal to the scorer and NEUTRAL_BULLISH to the gate. And engine.regime is
assigned in the second-to-last statement of OnTick while being read 980 lines earlier, so parts of
the system are working off last tick's answer.

I shipped two more fixes off that (the lot-sizing path was reading the wrong regime's stop
multiplier, and volatility spikes were being handed the most aggressive take-profit tier). Twelve
warrants today.

But I am ADOPTING its recommendation to hold the calibration re-run. Gates come from one
classifier, sizing and brackets from two others. A better number out of that would not be evidence
of a better system. Declare one authority first.

I also owe you a process note: I was editing the EA while that agent was auditing it. It caught
the file changing under it and re-verified everything, but that was my mistake.
